findings.evidence: grep: `NormEDS.lean:118-119` `have hfun : (universalNormEDS : ℤ → MvPolynomial NormEDSParam ℤ) = normEDS (X B) (X C) (X D) := funext universalNormEDS_apply`; `Invariant/NormEDS.lean:128-129` identical up to the `NormEDSParam.C` disambiguation. `Universal.lean:118` defines `universalNormEDS := normEDS (X B) (X C) (X D)` at function level, so the equation is `rfl` in that module.
findings.fix: Add the function-level equation to `Universal.lean` beside `universalNormEDS_apply`: `theorem universalNormEDS_eq : (universalNormEDS : ℤ → MvPolynomial NormEDSParam ℤ) = normEDS (X B) (X C) (X D) := rfl` (the body is in scope there, so `rfl` closes it; downstream it is unavailable, which is why both sites rebuild it). Then replace both `have hfun … := funext universalNormEDS_apply` blocks with `rw [universalNormEDS_eq]`.
findings.issue: The `hfun` block is a verbatim near-clone of `NormEDS.lean:118-119` — same statement, same proof `funext universalNormEDS_apply`. Repo-wide grep for `funext \w+_apply` returns exactly these two sites, both reconstructing the same function-level equation for `universalNormEDS` because only the pointwise `universalNormEDS_apply` is named.

summary: The three theorems are new material: Mathlib has no invarNum/invarDenom at all, and the b-cancellation genuinely cannot reuse invarNum_normEDS_one_eq_reducedInvarNum_mul, so the universal-transport route earns its place. One near-clone: the function-level unfolding of universalNormEDS is now hand-rolled in two files and should be a named lemma in Universal.lean.
